🇲🇽🏦 <u>MOODY'S FLAGS CONSUMER DEBT RISK FOR MEXICO'S BANKS — BUT HOUSEHOLD LEVERAGE STILL LOW VS THE REGION</u>

Moody's Ratings warns Mexico's banks face pressure from slow growth and rapidly expanding consumer credit: loan charge-offs are up nearly 100 basis points in three years, and CNBV data puts consumer delinquency at 3.35% in May — the highest for that month since 2021 — with credit cards at 3.51%, a 19-month high.

The context, from Moody's own report: household debt stands at 17.4% of GDP, still low against regional peers, and the worst deterioration in Latin America is Argentina's, where household defaults hit their highest level in over two decades. Milei's model, summed up in one number. (Source: El Financiero)

🇲🇽🥇 <u>MEXICO DOMINATES THE CENTRAL AMERICAN GAMES: 126 MEDALS, 49 GOLD — DOUBLE ITS NEAREST RIVAL</u>

Mexico is running away with the Central American and Caribbean Games in Santo Domingo: 126 medals — 49 gold, 45 silver, 32 bronze — against 84 for second-place Colombia and 48 for Cuba. One single day of competition brought 22 titles.

Rhythmic gymnastics swept all six golds on offer. Paulo Strehlke took the 1500m freestyle with a new Central American record, and the men's 4×200m relay set another regional mark at 7:15.9. World champion Yareli Acevedo added gold in the cycling omnium. And Mexico's stars in diving and athletics haven't even competed yet.

🇲🇽📺 <u>MEXICO OPENS PUBLIC CONSULTATION ON AUDIENCE RIGHTS IN RADIO & TV — SELF-REGULATION, NOT CENSORSHIP</u>

From July 27 to August 21, anyone — community radios, big broadcasters, ordinary citizens — can weigh in on the rules that will protect audience rights under Mexico's new Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law, via the Telecom Regulatory Commission's portal.

Sheinbaum's answer to the censorship chorus: "It's not about fining. The goal is a process of self-regulation — each medium names its own audience ombudsman." The draft guidelines: news clearly separated from opinion, editorial content from advertising, no false or decontextualized information, guaranteed right of reply, and accessibility for people with disabilities. The outlets that never worried about lying to their audiences are suddenly very concerned about "freedom."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SCAMMERS FORGE MEXICO'S ANTICORRUPTION SECRETARIAT DOCUMENTS TO EXTORT CITIZENS</u>

Mexico's Anticorruption and Good Government Secretariat is warning the public: criminals are circulating forged documents that ape the agency's letterhead and fake the signatures of Secretary Raquel Buenrostro and Undersecretary Alejandro Encinas.

The scheme: make victims believe there's an investigation against them, then demand money "to avoid supposed legal consequences." The agency's statement is blunt — the documents are "completely false, were not issued by this secretariat, and lack all official validity." Any request for payment or deposits is a fraud. Verify only through official channels — and never pay.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>25 RIGHT-WING EX-PRESIDENTS RUSH TO DEFEND HUACHICOL MAGNATE — SHEINBAUM: THIS IS CRIMINAL, NOT POLITICAL</u>

Twenty-five right-wing ex-presidents from Mexico, Spain and Latin America — the so-called Grupo IDEA — signed a letter calling Ernesto Ruffo's arrest "political vengeance." Sheinbaum's answer: "It has nothing to do with a political matter, it's a criminal matter."

The FGR built 96 pieces of evidence — chemistry, mechanical and electrical engineering, criminalistics — against the main shareholder of a company that imported fuel while declaring less than it brought in, or calling it something else. Thirty rail tankers seized. The old guard defending its own, once again.
